FX-TDIFF-001.says: As added: the layer against itself now, so nothing differs and every pixel that shows is black, the clear ones clear.

FX-TDIFF-002.says: Against itself one frame back: the ball's old and new places show, the rest is black. At frame 0 the frame before is outside the layer, a clear target, so the layer shows as it is.

FX-TDIFF-003.says: Against itself one frame ahead. At frame 4 the next frame holds the same drawing, so all black; at frame 7 the next frame is past the out point, so the layer as it is.

FX-TDIFF-004.says: Absolute Difference off, one frame back: no difference is mid grey, lighter where the layer is lighter now, darker where it was lighter.

FX-TDIFF-005.says: Contrast 20, one frame back: every difference three times as strong, held at white.

FX-TDIFF-006.says: Alpha Channel Target, one frame back: the covering is the target's, so the ball's old place on the stripe shows and its new place does not.

FX-TDIFF-007.says: Alpha Channel Blend: the mean of the two coverings.

FX-TDIFF-008.says: Alpha Channel Max: the larger of the two coverings.

FX-TDIFF-009.says: Alpha Channel Full On: every pixel covered, the clear corner black.

FX-TDIFF-010.says: Alpha Channel Lightness Of Result: covered as far as the difference is light, so the still background goes clear.

FX-TDIFF-011.says: Alpha Channel Max Of Result: covered by the strongest channel of the difference.

FX-TDIFF-012.says: Alpha Channel Alpha Difference: covered by how much the covering changed, only on the stripe where the ball came and went.

FX-TDIFF-013.says: Alpha Channel Alpha Difference Only: as FX-TDIFF-012, with every colour white.

FX-TDIFF-014.says: The plate as the target, now: the background matches and goes black, only the ball and its trail show.

FX-TDIFF-015.says: The plate from frame 4 as the target: at frame 2 it is clear, so the layer shows as it is; at frame 4 it is FX-TDIFF-014.

FX-TDIFF-016.says: A layer that is not in the composition, `gone`: nothing changes, and the warning every frame.

FX-TDIFF-017.says: A second layer of the same drawings as the target, one frame back: FX-TDIFF-002.

FX-TDIFF-018.says: Time Offset keyed from 0 at frame 0 to -4 frames at frame 4: at frame 0 black; at frame 2 two frames back; at frame 4 four frames back.

FX-TDIFF-019.says: FX-TDIFF-002 on the holder moved 2 right and 1 down: the same picture moved, since the target lies on the layer.

FX-TDIFF-020.says: An Exposure of +1 before Time Difference, against itself now: the target is the drawing without its effects, so the brightening shows as a difference.

FX-TDIFF-021.says: FX-TDIFF-004 with an Exposure of -1 after Time Difference: the grey picture darkened.

FX-TDIFF-022.says: On an adjustment layer above the holder with no target named: an adjustment layer has no picture of its own, so nothing changes.

FX-TDIFF-023.says: On an adjustment layer with the plate as the target: the frame beneath, here the holder's own rectangle, against the plate, FX-TDIFF-014.

FX-TDIFF-024.says: Contrast 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-TDIFF-025.says: Contrast -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-TDIFF-026.says: Time Offset 61 seconds, above 60. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-TDIFF-027.says: Time Offset -61 seconds, below -60. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-TDIFF-028.says: An Alpha Channel written "lightness". The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-TDIFF-029.says: An Absolute Difference written "maybe". The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-TDIFF-030.says: A target written as the number 3, not a word. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-TDIFF-031.says: Time Offset keyed to 100 seconds at frame 4. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

cycle_two.json.says: `a` and `b`, each the ball, each with a Time Difference whose target is the other: refused, `EFFECT_LAYER_CYCLE`.
